mainTopic: The reasons of רבה (לשמה) and רבא (קיום) for the declaration 'בפני נכתב ובפני נחתם', their practical differences, and why a single שליח is enough according to רבה
overview: The amud opens at the end of רבה's explanation: a שליח bringing a גט from מדינת הים must say 'בפני נכתב ובפני נחתם' because people overseas are not experts in writing a גט לשמה. רבא gives a different reason: no witnesses are available there to confirm the signatures (קיום). The גמרא then lists three cases where the two reasons lead to different results: two people bring the גט, a גט goes from region to region inside ארץ ישראל, and a גט stays within one region overseas. Next the גמרא challenges רבה: if the declaration is testimony about לשמה, it should need two witnesses. The first answer is that one witness is believed about איסורין. The גמרא rejects that answer, because a married woman is an established prohibition of ערוה, and such a matter needs two witnesses. The second answer is that most people are experts in לשמה. Even רבי מאיר, who worries about the minority, agrees, since court scribes know the rule, so the declaration is only a requirement of the רבנן. The explanation of why the רבנן accepted one person begins with 'והכא' and continues on the next amud.

steps.title: רבה's reason: they are not experts in writing for her sake
steps.stepSummary: רבה explains that the שליח must declare 'בפני נכתב ובפני נחתם' because people overseas are not experts in writing a גט לשמה.
steps.simpleTranslation: Because they are not experts in writing it for her sake.
steps.whatsHappening: We are finishing רבה's explanation of why a שליח bringing a גט from overseas must say it was written and signed in front of him. His reason is that people there do not know the rule of לשמה.
steps.deeperAnalysis: A גט must be written specifically for this husband and this wife (לשמה). רבה worries that people in מדינת הים do not know this rule. The שליח's declaration works as testimony that the גט was written and signed לשמה.

keyTerms.meaning: experts; people who know the rules well
for her sake; written specifically for this woman
'It was written in front of me and signed in front of me', the שליח's declaration

phrases.english: Because they are not experts in writing it for her sake.
phrases.notes: 'They' means the people living overseas. This line finishes רבה's answer, which started just before.

steps.relationToPreviousStep: Finishes רבה's answer to the earlier question of why the declaration is needed.
steps.mimraCoreRuling: The declaration is needed because people overseas may not know that a גט must be written לשמה.

steps.title: רבא's reason: no witnesses available to confirm it
steps.stepSummary: רבא disagrees with רבה's reason. He says the declaration is needed because no witnesses are around to confirm the signatures on a גט from far away.
steps.simpleTranslation: רבא says: because witnesses are not available to confirm it.
steps.whatsHappening: רבא gives a different reason for the same rule. He worries that nobody will be able to confirm the signatures on the גט.
steps.deeperAnalysis: Normally a document can be challenged, and then witnesses must confirm the signatures (קיום). A גט from far away has no such witnesses nearby, so the husband could later claim it is forged. The שליח's declaration stands in for that confirmation, so רבא's concern is about proving the גט is real, not about לשמה.

keyTerms.meaning: witnesses who are available and easy to find
to confirm it; to verify the signatures on the document (קִיּוּם)

steps.whyThisMatters: From here on, the sugya works with two different concerns, לשמה and קיום. Each case that follows is tested against both.

phrases.english: Rava says:
Because witnesses are not available to confirm it.
phrases.notes: 'Confirm it' means proving that the signatures on the גט are real, in case someone later says it is forged.

steps.relationToPreviousStep: A second, competing explanation for the same rule.
steps.mimraCoreRuling: The declaration is needed because no witnesses are available to do קיום on the גט.

steps.title: What is the practical difference between them?
steps.stepSummary: The גמרא asks in which case the reasons of רבה and רבא would lead to different results.
steps.simpleTranslation: What is the difference between them?
steps.whatsHappening: The גמרא asks how the two reasons differ in practice. This line sets up the list of cases that comes next.
steps.deeperAnalysis: Both reasons explain the same rule, so the גמרא wants a case where only one of the two concerns applies. In such a case, one view would still require the declaration and the other would not.

keyTerms.meaning: what is the difference between them? (in practice)

phrases.english: What is the difference between them?

steps.relationToPreviousStep: Compares the two reasons just given.
steps.sheelahInformationSought: A case where the reasons of רבה and רבא lead to different results.

steps.title: First difference: two people brought the גט
steps.stepSummary: If two people bring the גט, there are already two witnesses to confirm it. רבא's concern is gone, but רבה's concern about לשמה remains.
steps.simpleTranslation: There is a difference between them where two people brought it.
steps.whatsHappening: The גמרא gives its first case: two people bring the גט together. Under רבא's reason the declaration may not be needed, but under רבה's reason it still is.
steps.deeperAnalysis: Two bringers are themselves a pair of witnesses who can confirm the גט, so רבא's worry about קיום is solved. They do not prove it was written לשמה, so according to רבה they must still make the declaration.

keyTerms.meaning: there is a difference between them
two people

phrases.english: There is a difference between them
where two people brought it.
phrases.notes: 'It' is the גט, and two people bringing it are already a pair of witnesses.

steps.teshuvahAnswerProvided: When two people bring the גט, רבא's קיום concern is solved but רבה's לשמה concern remains.

steps.title: Second difference: from region to region inside ארץ ישראל
steps.stepSummary: If a גט is brought from one region to another within ארץ ישראל, people there know the rule of לשמה, but witnesses may still be unavailable.
steps.simpleTranslation: Alternatively, from one region to another region in ארץ ישראל.
steps.whatsHappening: The גמרא gives a second case. A גט travels between regions inside ארץ ישראל, and here רבא would require the declaration while רבה would not.
steps.deeperAnalysis: People in ארץ ישראל know how to write a גט לשמה, so רבה has no concern. Between distant regions, witnesses to confirm the signatures are still hard to find, so רבא's concern remains.

keyTerms.meaning: alternatively; or another possibility
from one region to another region

phrases.english: Alternatively, from one region to another region
in Eretz Yisrael.

steps.triggerLanguage: אִי נָמֵי, מִמְּדִינָה לִמְדִינָה בְּאֶרֶץ יִשְׂרָאֵל
steps.relationToPreviousStep: A second, alternative answer to the question of step 3.
steps.teshuvahAnswerProvided: Between regions in ארץ ישראל there is no לשמה concern, but the קיום concern remains, so רבא requires the declaration and רבה does not.

steps.title: Third difference: within the same region overseas
steps.stepSummary: If a גט is brought within a single region overseas, witnesses are nearby, but people there still do not know the rule of לשמה.
steps.simpleTranslation: Alternatively, within that same region overseas.
steps.whatsHappening: The גמרא gives a third case, the reverse of the second one. Here רבה would require the declaration and רבא would not.
steps.deeperAnalysis: Inside one region, witnesses who know the signatures are close by, so רבא's קיום concern is gone. The people are still overseas and may not know the rule of לשמה, so רבה's concern remains.

keyTerms.meaning: in that same region
overseas lands; places outside ארץ ישראל

steps.whatToRemember: רבה's concern is לשמה and רבא's concern is קיום. Each of the three cases removes one concern and leaves the other: two bringers, region to region in ארץ ישראל, and one region overseas.
steps.confusionAlert: Do not mix up cases 2 and 3. Inside ארץ ישראל, only רבא requires the declaration. Within one region overseas, only רבה requires it.

phrases.english: Alternatively, within that same region
in a land overseas.

steps.triggerLanguage: אִי נָמֵי, בְּאוֹתָהּ מְדִינָה בִּמְדִינַת הַיָּם
steps.relationToPreviousStep: A third alternative answer, the mirror image of step 5.
steps.teshuvahAnswerProvided: Within one region overseas, witnesses are available, so רבא has no concern, but רבה's לשמה concern remains.

steps.title: According to רבה, two witnesses should be needed
steps.stepSummary: The גמרא challenges רבה: if the declaration is testimony about לשמה, it should need two witnesses like every testimony in the תורה.
steps.simpleTranslation: According to רבה, who said the reason is that people are not experts in writing a גט for her sake, we should need two people to testify, just like every other testimony in the תורה!
steps.whatsHappening: The גמרא attacks רבה's reason. If the שליח's declaration is really testimony that the גט was written לשמה, one person should not be enough.
steps.deeperAnalysis: For רבא, the declaration replaces the confirmation of the signatures. For רבה, it is testimony about how the גט was written. Normally the תורה requires two witnesses for testimony, yet our משנה lets one שליח bring the גט.

keyTerms.meaning: Let us require two (witnesses)
Just like, the same as
Testimonies in the תורה, which normally need two witnesses
Experts, people who know the rule

phrases.english: And according to Rabba, who said
that it is because they are not experts in writing for her sake
let us require two
phrases.notes: He means two people should have to make the declaration, the way two witnesses testify.

phrases.english: just as with all testimonies in the Torah!

steps.triggerLanguage: וּלְרַבָּה דְּאָמַר לְפִי שֶׁאֵין בְּקִיאִין לִשְׁמָהּ לִיבְעֵי תְּרֵי
steps.relationToPreviousStep: After the differences between רבה and רבא are listed, the גמרא challenges רבה's reason on its own terms.
steps.kashyaTarget: רבה's reason that the declaration is about לשמה
steps.kashyaAttackLogic: If the declaration is testimony, it should follow the normal rule that testimony needs two witnesses. Yet the משנה accepts one שליח.

steps.title: One witness is believed about prohibitions
steps.stepSummary: The answer: in questions of what is forbidden or permitted, one witness is believed.
steps.simpleTranslation: One witness is believed in matters of prohibition.
steps.whatsHappening: The גמרא answers that two witnesses are not needed here, because one witness is trusted about איסורין.
steps.deeperAnalysis: Testimony about money or punishments needs two witnesses. But when the question is only whether something is permitted or forbidden, one reliable person is enough. The גמרא treats the declaration about לשמה as this kind of testimony.

keyTerms.meaning: One witness
Believed, trusted
Matters of what is forbidden or permitted

phrases.english: One witness is believed regarding prohibitions.

steps.terutzResolutionType: Recategorizes the testimony as a matter of איסורין, where one witness is enough
steps.terutzHavaAmina: The declaration is testimony, so it needs two witnesses.
steps.terutzMaskana: It is testimony about איסורין, so one witness is believed.

steps.title: A married woman is an established prohibition, so two witnesses are needed
steps.stepSummary: The גמרא rejects the comparison: one witness is believed only when no prohibition was established, but a married woman is an established דבר שבערוה, which needs two.
steps.simpleTranslation: You can say one witness is believed about prohibitions in a case like a piece of fat that might be forbidden חלב or might be permitted fat, since no prohibition was ever established. But here the prohibition of a married woman is established, so it is a matter of ערוה, and a matter of ערוה needs at least two witnesses!
steps.whatsHappening: The גמרא pushes back on the answer. The rule of עד אחד works for an unclear piece of fat, but not for releasing a married woman.
steps.deeperAnalysis: Two differences are given. With the fat, nothing was ever known to be forbidden, but this woman is definitely forbidden right now as an אשת איש. Also, matters of ערוה have their own rule: they always need two witnesses.

keyTerms.meaning: Forbidden fat
Permitted fat
A prohibition was established (there is a known forbidden status)
A married woman
A matter of forbidden relationships

steps.confusionAlert: Don't think the גמרא is rejecting the rule of עד אחד נאמן באיסורין. The rule stays true; the גמרא is only saying it does not cover our case of an established prohibition of ערוה.

phrases.english: Say that we do say
one witness is believed regarding prohibitions
in a case such as a piece of fat

phrases.aramaic: סָפֵק שֶׁל חֵלֶב סָפֵק שֶׁל שׁוּמָּן,
phrases.english: which may be forbidden fat and may be permitted fat
where no prohibition was established

phrases.aramaic: אֲבָל הָכָא, דְּאִיתַּחְזַק אִיסּוּרָא דְּאֵשֶׁת אִישׁ,
phrases.english: but here, where the prohibition of a married woman is established
it is a matter of forbidden relations
and a matter of forbidden relations cannot be established by fewer than two!

steps.triggerLanguage: אֵימוֹר דְּאָמְרִינַן עֵד אֶחָד נֶאֱמָן בְּאִיסּוּרִין
steps.relationToPreviousStep: Rejects the answer of step 8 by limiting it to cases with no established prohibition.
steps.kashyaTarget: The answer that עד אחד נאמן באיסורין covers the declaration
steps.kashyaAttackLogic: One witness is believed only when there is no established prohibition. A married woman has an established prohibition of ערוה, which needs two witnesses.

steps.title: Most people are experts in writing לשמה
steps.stepSummary: The answer: most people already know the rule of לשמה, so the declaration is not real testimony that needs two.
steps.whatsHappening: The גמרא gives a new answer. We are not really unsure whether the גט was written לשמה, because most people know this rule.
steps.deeperAnalysis: The challenge in step 9 assumed the declaration was what took away the woman's married status. Now the גמרא says the majority already shows the גט was written properly. So the declaration is not the main proof, and the rule needing two witnesses does not apply.

keyTerms.meaning: The majority

phrases.english: Most are experts.
phrases.notes: He means most people writing a גט know it must be written for this specific woman.

steps.relationToPreviousStep: Answers the challenge of step 9 with a new approach.
steps.terutzResolutionType: Relies on רוב, so there is no real doubt needing two witnesses
steps.terutzHavaAmina: The declaration is the only thing that permits a married woman, so two are needed.
steps.terutzMaskana: The majority already makes the גט valid; the declaration only adds to it.

steps.title: Even רבי מאיר agrees, since court scribes know the rule
steps.stepSummary: Even רבי מאיר, who worries about the minority, agrees here, because court scribes surely know the rule. The declaration is only a rabbinic extra.
steps.simpleTranslation: And even according to רבי מאיר, who worries about the minority, ordinary scribes of the judges are surely learned, and it was the רבנן who required the declaration. And here...
steps.whatsHappening: The גמרא strengthens its answer: even someone who worries about the small minority would agree here. The sentence then continues into the next part of the daf.
steps.deeperAnalysis: רבי מאיר usually does not rely on the majority. But גיטין are written by professional court scribes, who definitely know the rule of לשמה. So the declaration is only a rabbinic requirement. The words 'וְהָכָא' begin the explanation of why the רבנן were lenient and accepted one person, and that explanation continues on the next amud.

keyTerms.meaning: Worries about the minority
Scribes who work for the judges
It is the רבנן who required it (only a rabbinic rule)

steps.whatToRemember: According to רבה, the guarantee that the גט was written לשמה comes from the fact that scribes know the rule. The declaration בפני נכתב is only an extra safeguard added by the רבנן. The words 'וְהָכָא' begin the explanation, which continues on the next amud, of why one שליח is enough.

phrases.english: And even according to Rabbi Meir
who worries about the minority
ordinary scribes of the judges
are certainly learned
and it is the Sages who required it
and here

steps.relationToPreviousStep: Extends the answer of step 10 so it works even for רבי מאיר.
steps.terutzResolutionType: Shows the declaration is only rabbinic, since even the minority concern does not apply to court scribes
steps.terutzHavaAmina: רבי מאיר, who worries about the minority, would need real testimony from two witnesses.
steps.terutzMaskana: Court scribes all know the rule, so the declaration is only a rabbinic extra and one person is enough.
